evidence_items.title: Faction slogans do not supply a complete party map
evidence_items.description: First Corinthians reports name-based slogans around Paul, Apollos, Cephas, and Christ while appealing against divisions.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The slogans are directly inspectable, but their speakers, durability, and social organization remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents reconstructing rigid parties or using unity language to silence a substantiated complaint.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul reports slogans and quarrels and appeals for shared purpose.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Deliberative and honor-conflict readings explain aspects of the rhetoric without proving a complete faction system.

temporal_scope.notes: Direct-letter evidence; party reconstruction remains approximate.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The passage directly names slogans, quarrels, and the anti-division appeal.

evidence_items.notes: Unity cannot mean suppression of truthful reporting, dissent, or survivor testimony.

evidence_items.title: Chloe's people form a named reporting channel
evidence_items.description: Paul says Chloe's people informed him of quarrels in Corinth, while their roles and the report process remain unstated.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The report source is explicit; identity, consent, procedure, and subsequent risk are unknown.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Makes mediated reporting visible and rejects punishing reporters merely for bringing conflict to attention.
evidence_items.primary_observation: A named network conveys a conflict report to an absent apostle.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The verse may illuminate information networks but cannot establish a complete complaint procedure.

temporal_scope.notes: The direct letter preserves only Paul's attribution.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Names the reporting source while leaving process and risk unreported.

evidence_items.notes: A reporter is not disloyal merely because a disclosure affects institutional reputation.

evidence_items.title: The cross reverses status competition
evidence_items.description: Paul contrasts the word of the cross with status-producing wisdom and relocates boasting in the Lord.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The literary contrast is strong; precise social groups and rhetorical models remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Constrains leadership prestige, educational elitism, and claims that public success proves divine approval.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Cross, calling, weakness, and boasting language form one status-reversing unit.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Honor-conflict analysis can clarify the reversal without reducing theology to social competition.

temporal_scope.notes: Social interpretation remains bounded by the letter's theological argument.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly connects the cross, divine choice, human status, and boasting.

evidence_items.notes: Cross-shaped weakness cannot be used to romanticize abuse or demand silent suffering.

evidence_items.title: Paul and Apollos are servants, not owners
evidence_items.description: Paul and Apollos are servants through whom the audience believed, while God gives growth.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The servant and growth language is direct even though the coworker grammar is discussed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects founder ownership of communities and treats leader rivalry as a category error.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Human agents plant and water; divine agency supplies growth.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The agricultural metaphor relativizes leaders without denying differentiated labor.

temporal_scope.notes: Direct metaphor in an occasional letter.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly subordinates Paul and Apollos to divine growth.

evidence_items.notes: No founder acquires people, assets, testimony, or perpetual control.

evidence_items.title: Apostolic service remains under judgment
evidence_items.description: Paul resists premature verdicts while placing hidden motives and his own stewardship under the Lord's future judgment.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The eschatological frame is explicit; its relation to present investigation needs careful distinction.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Denies finalizing rumor while also denying that leaders are accountable only to themselves.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul neither absolutizes human approval nor exempts his ministry from evaluation.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Future judgment cannot be invoked to obstruct present safeguarding, evidence preservation, or lawful accountability.

temporal_scope.notes: Modern procedure is analogical, not described.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Places ministry under divine examination without licensing baseless verdicts.

evidence_items.notes: Do not confuse due process with deferment until an afterlife.

evidence_items.title: Not beyond what is written remains disputed
evidence_items.description: Paul applies an opaque formula so that nobody is puffed up for one person against another.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The anti-boasting purpose is visible, but the formula's referent and exact force are highly disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Supports humility while preventing the uncertain phrase from becoming an unrestricted compliance rule.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The formula is joined to a warning against interpersonal status inflation.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Proposals include cited scripture, proverbial instruction, or prior letter language; none securely creates a modern policy.

temporal_scope.notes: Lexical and referential uncertainty must remain explicit.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins the formula to anti-boasting purpose.

evidence_items.notes: Never use an uncertain formula to suppress questions, evidence, or appeal.

evidence_items.title: Apostolic irony exposes status claims
evidence_items.description: Paul depicts apostles as spectacle, fools, weak, dishonored, hungry, poorly clothed, beaten, homeless, and laboring.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The catalogue is direct; irony, exaggeration, and social function remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Exposes triumphalist credential claims without making deprivation or assault a leadership qualification.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Sharp contrasts pit Corinthian self-satisfaction against apostolic abasement.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient irony and honor reversal illuminate rhetoric; reported harm still requires worker safety rather than imitation.

temporal_scope.notes: Rhetorical force does not establish a harm quota.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The passage supplies a status-reversing hardship catalogue.

evidence_items.notes: Do not recruit, retain, or shame workers by demanding apostolic misery.

evidence_items.title: Parental admonition does not infantilize adults
evidence_items.description: Paul uses father language, admonition, imitation, Timothy's visit, love, and a threatened choice between rod and gentleness.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The metaphor and rhetorical alternatives are explicit; ancient household resonances and modern transfer are disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Keeps correction relational while rejecting infantilization, corporal punishment, loyalty demands, and parental ownership of adults.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Parental language intensifies Paul's founder appeal within a contested relationship.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The metaphor can express care and generation without conferring household-head powers on leaders.

temporal_scope.notes: Ancient kinship metaphor requires consent and safeguarding controls today.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins parental metaphor, admonition, delegated reminder, and rhetorical alternatives.

evidence_items.notes: The rod image cannot authorize physical, emotional, financial, or spiritual violence.

evidence_items.title: The Corinthian sexual case has missing voices
evidence_items.description: Paul addresses a reported ongoing relationship with a father's wife, but the woman is not addressed and her status, voice, consent, and safety are unknown.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The reported relationship is clear; identity, household dynamics, coercion, and absent testimony cannot be recovered.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires safeguarding inquiry into power and consent rather than treating the passage as a complete case file.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Only the man and the assembly receive explicit instruction in the surviving passage.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Proposals about stepmother, concubine, membership, and status remain historical reconstructions.

temporal_scope.notes: The letter is not an investigative transcript.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Names the report while leaving the woman's voice and key safety facts absent.

evidence_items.notes: Do not assign blame, compel contact, or bypass mandatory reporting from absent data.

evidence_items.title: Mourning and removal remain case-bound and disputed
evidence_items.description: Paul calls for mourning, removal, and handing the man to Satan with an expressed salvation aim.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The action and stated aim are explicit; physical exclusion, spiritual exposure, duration, and effects remain deeply disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents a difficult ancient action from becoming automatic permanent expulsion, deprivation, or punishment without review.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The community is addressed collectively about a specified reported case.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Competing readings concern exclusion, spiritual protection, affliction, repentance, and eschatological rescue.

temporal_scope.notes: No complete procedure, duration, or modern sanction is supplied.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The passage directly presents mourning, assembly action, and a restorative horizon.

evidence_items.notes: Never coordinate housing, employment, family, medical, or social deprivation as a religious sanction.

evidence_items.title: Inside and outside judgment are distinguished
evidence_items.description: Paul limits the current instruction to community insiders and rejects judging outsiders in the same way.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The distinction is explicit; membership boundaries and modern institutional scope remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Blocks policing of outsiders and limits community authority to genuinely voluntary, bounded participation.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Insider differentiation and outsider nonjudgment occur in the same argument.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient assembly boundaries do not confer civil power or control over former members, relatives, or dependents.

temporal_scope.notes: Modern membership must remain voluntary and legally bounded.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly distinguishes those inside and outside the community.

evidence_items.notes: Leaving a community does not authorize pursuit, surveillance, blacklisting, or family coercion.

evidence_items.title: Lawsuit critique does not conceal abuse
evidence_items.description: Paul criticizes insider status litigation while also condemning wrongdoing and defrauding within the community.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Both elements are direct; the dispute type, court context, and modern legal transfer are debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Distinguishes voluntary mediation of suitable disputes from crimes, abuse, safety threats, mandatory reporting, and access to courts.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The passage rebukes both litigation and perpetrators of wrong and fraud.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Roman status competition may contextualize the appeal, but internal process cannot become concealment.

temporal_scope.notes: Current law and qualified safeguarding expertise govern reporting.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Keeps litigation critique beside explicit condemnation of harm and fraud.

evidence_items.notes: Never force mediation or religious arbitration on a harmed person.

evidence_items.title: Gifts serve the common good
evidence_items.description: Different gifts, services, and workings are attributed to one Spirit, Lord, and God and are given for the common good.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The common-good purpose and differentiation are directly stated; gift taxonomy remains discussed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Tests authority claims by communal benefit rather than charisma, office, performance, or claimed revelation.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Plural gifts are not private possessions and do not erase communal discernment.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The common good is a strong ethical control but not a substitute for fact-finding or individual rights.

temporal_scope.notes: Direct theological claim in an occasional assembly argument.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly gives differentiated gifts a common-good purpose.

evidence_items.notes: Claimed gifting never defeats consent, safety, access, competence, or accountability.

evidence_items.title: Table inequality humiliates those with nothing
evidence_items.description: Paul says unequal eating means the gathering is not the Lord's Supper and asks whether the assembly humiliates those who have nothing.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Humiliation and unequal consumption are explicit; room layout, meal sequence, and class composition remain reconstructed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Makes material exclusion and public shame accountability concerns rather than acceptable tools of correction.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Food disparity, intoxication, hunger, and humiliation are addressed together.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Household and status models illuminate the scene without proving one architectural arrangement.

temporal_scope.notes: Material setting remains partly reconstructed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly identifies humiliation of those lacking food.

evidence_items.notes: Food, sacraments, disability accommodations, or essential aid must not be leverage for compliance.

evidence_items.title: Members called weaker receive greater honor
evidence_items.description: The body metaphor calls apparently weaker members necessary and directs greater honor and care toward less honored parts.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The status reversal is explicit; identification of particular members and modern embodiment transfer remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Supports disability access and protection of marginalized members rather than paternalism or exclusion.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Difference, necessity, special honor, mutual care, and shared suffering occur in one metaphor.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The metaphor challenges hierarchy but must not erase individual agency or label disabled people weak.

temporal_scope.notes: Contemporary disability language must not be projected backward.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins necessary membership, honor, care, suffering, and rejoicing.

evidence_items.notes: Provide accessible communication, process modifications, support persons, and equal voice.

evidence_items.title: Prophecy remains subject to plural weighing
evidence_items.description: Two or three prophets may speak and others are to weigh what is said; a claimed revelation does not end discernment.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Plural speech and weighing are direct; who weighs and how remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects leader revelation as immunity from questions, evidence, independent review, or correction.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Speech, weighing, turn-taking, learning, encouragement, and peace appear together.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Assembly-order readings differ, but the text does not establish one unreviewable prophetic office.

temporal_scope.notes: Local procedure is not recoverable in full.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly requires plural weighing of prophetic speech.

evidence_items.notes: Discernment must include conflict-of-interest controls and accessible ways to dissent.

evidence_items.title: Order serves participation, learning, and peace
evidence_items.description: The assembly-order argument repeatedly names edification, intelligibility, learning, encouragement, self-control, and peace.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The repeated purposes are direct; textual and gender-related disputes prevent a single blueprint.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents order language from becoming leader convenience, forced silence, or suppression of necessary conflict.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Order is justified by communal goods rather than by one speaker's status.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Rhetorical and textual disputes, especially around verses 34-35, require explicit qualification.

temporal_scope.notes: Textual placement and application remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The unit directly links order to participation, intelligibility, edification, and peace.

evidence_items.notes: Peace is not the absence of reports, questions, grief, or justified protest.

evidence_items.title: Love governs gifts and conflict
evidence_items.description: Love is patient and kind, does not insist on its own way, does not rejoice in wrongdoing, and rejoices with truth.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The predicates and literary placement are direct; modern relational slogans can still distort them.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Makes truth, patience, and noncoercion controls on correction, gifts, leadership, and reconciliation.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The love discourse stands between gift ranking and assembly-order instruction.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Its communal location resists reducing it to romantic sentiment or using endurance to keep someone unsafe.

temporal_scope.notes: Direct ethical rhetoric with broad but bounded canonical reception.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Literary placement makes love a control on status and speech.

evidence_items.notes: Love never requires concealment, forced contact, endurance of abuse, or abandonment of due process.

evidence_items.title: Comfort circulates through affliction
evidence_items.description: Second Corinthians presents comfort received from God as enabling comfort of others and invites shared reliance rather than leader self-sufficiency.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Reciprocal comfort is explicit; the Asian affliction and exact community experience remain uncertain.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Centers care and mutual aid without making suffering a credential or pressuring disclosure.
evidence_items.primary_observation: God, the letter writers, and communities are connected through affliction, comfort, prayer, and hope.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The passage may frame later conflict repair while not supplying clinical trauma theory.

temporal_scope.notes: The direct letter does not identify the affliction in full.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly describes reciprocal comfort, prayer, danger, and reliance.

evidence_items.notes: Support must remain consent-based and may include qualified medical or mental-health care.

evidence_items.title: Changed plans expose contested impact
evidence_items.description: Paul defends altered travel intentions and says he avoided another visit to spare the Corinthians.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The defense and sparing claim are explicit; chronology, prior commitments, and recipient impact remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires leaders to explain changed commitments and assess impact without claiming infallible intention.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Travel plans, accusations of vacillation, oath language, sparing, and grief form one contested relationship sequence.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Apologetic-rhetorical readings clarify self-defense but cannot recover every visit or response.

temporal_scope.notes: Visit and letter sequences remain reconstructed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly defends a changed itinerary in a damaged relationship.

evidence_items.notes: Good intent does not cancel repair, disclosure, or governance review when plans cause harm.

evidence_items.title: Paul denies lordship over faith
evidence_items.description: Paul explicitly says the writers do not lord it over the Corinthians' faith but work with them for joy.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The denial and coworker claim are direct; their full rhetorical effect remains discussed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Directly rejects founder domination, coerced belief, and apostolic immunity.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Apostolic defense includes an explicit non-domination boundary.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The statement does not remove all authority but makes ownership of another's faith illegitimate.

temporal_scope.notes: Direct letter evidence within apologetic rhetoric.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly denies lordship and asserts coworking for joy.

evidence_items.notes: No spiritual office grants control of conscience, reporting, medical care, finances, housing, or relationships.

evidence_items.title: Tearful intent does not erase impact
evidence_items.description: Paul describes writing through affliction, anguish, and tears so that abundant love would be known.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Emotion and stated intent are direct; the lost letter, its wording, and recipient experience are unavailable.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Distinguishes a writer's loving intent from the impact, proportionality, and safety of communication.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul retrospectively explains an earlier painful communication.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Reconstructed painful-letter sequences vary, and emotional sincerity cannot settle whether a method was appropriate.

temporal_scope.notes: The earlier letter is not preserved independently.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly states the writer's emotions and intended disclosure of love.

evidence_items.notes: Trauma-aware communication avoids surprise confrontation, coercive intensity, and demands for immediate response.

evidence_items.title: Majority punishment leaves process gaps
evidence_items.description: Paul calls a punishment by the majority sufficient without naming the offender, offense, decision rule, minority, duration, or safeguards.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Majority and sufficiency language is direct; identity and procedure are uncertain.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents majority status from substituting for impartial evidence, minority protection, appeal, or review.
evidence_items.primary_observation: A prior collective action is reassessed as sufficient.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The offender's identification with 1 Corinthians 5 is common but not certain.

temporal_scope.notes: No complete case record survives.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly refers to majority action and its sufficiency.

evidence_items.notes: A vote cannot establish facts when power, retaliation, inaccessible process, or conflicts of interest distort participation.

evidence_items.title: Forgiveness and comfort prevent excessive grief
evidence_items.description: Paul urges forgiveness and comfort so that the person is not swallowed by excessive grief.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The restorative aim is direct; person, offense, and exact reintegration remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Makes duration, mental wellbeing, proportionality, and reassessment part of disciplinary accountability.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The community's prior action is followed by a call to change course.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Forgiveness and comfort indicate restoration but do not automatically answer questions of trust, office, access, restitution, or contact.

temporal_scope.notes: Modern mental-health claims require qualified expertise.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly links changed communal action to preventing excessive grief.

evidence_items.notes: Care for the disciplined person cannot displace survivor safety, restitution, or fact-based risk assessment.

evidence_items.title: A boundary is reassessed and love reaffirmed
evidence_items.description: Paul calls the earlier action sufficient and asks the community to reaffirm love and forgive.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Reassessment and reaffirmation are direct; exact restoration terms are not.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Supports proportionate, time-bounded, reviewable action instead of permanent ostracism.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The requested community response changes after an earlier sanction.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The text supports revisability without proving automatic reinstatement to leadership or unrestricted access.

temporal_scope.notes: Person and prior action remain partly unknown.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly changes the community's requested posture after sufficient action.

evidence_items.notes: Restoration may mean safe belonging or care without office, unsupervised access, or forced contact.

evidence_items.title: Proclamation remains under integrity scrutiny
evidence_items.description: Paul contrasts sincerity before God with peddling God's word and speaks within a contested defense of ministry.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The contrast is direct; economic nuance and rival referents remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Subjects spiritual messaging, financial interest, and self-presentation to transparency rather than assumed purity.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The writer advances a moral contrast while defending his public role.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient peddling language may concern commercialization or corruption; it does not let a leader certify their own motives.

temporal_scope.notes: Opponent and economic reconstruction remain bounded.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly contrasts sincere speech and peddling within apostolic defense.

evidence_items.notes: Independent financial and conduct review is compatible with sincere ministry.

evidence_items.title: Living-letter language does not own people
evidence_items.description: Paul calls the Corinthians a letter written on hearts while denying self-sufficient competence and attributing sufficiency to God.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The metaphor and divine-sufficiency claim are direct; recommendation practices and polemical target remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Limits leaders from using community outcomes, testimonies, or changed lives as proprietary credentials.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Commendation, community embodiment, and divine sufficiency are rhetorically joined.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient recommendation-letter comparison helps explain the metaphor without granting control over members' stories.

temporal_scope.notes: Social practice remains reconstructed from broader evidence.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly combines recommendation metaphor and divine sufficiency.

evidence_items.notes: Obtain consent before publicizing testimony; respect withdrawal and confidentiality.

evidence_items.title: Treasure in fragile vessels limits leader power
evidence_items.description: The earthen-vessel image attributes extraordinary power to God and not to the human messenger amid affliction.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The power contrast is direct; embodiment and rhetorical applications remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects leader invulnerability and the claim that surviving hardship proves superior authority.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Fragility and divine power coexist without the vessel becoming the source.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Weakness rhetoric can destabilize triumphalism but must not excuse incapacity, conceal misconduct, or demand harm.

temporal_scope.notes: Modern disability and trauma categories are not projected into the image.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly distinguishes divine power from the fragile messenger.

evidence_items.notes: Fragility merits support and access; it is not immunity from role-specific competence or conduct review.

evidence_items.title: Apostolic commendation is contested
evidence_items.description: Second Corinthians repeatedly addresses self-commendation, comparison, approved limits, and boasting in the Lord.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The repeated vocabulary is direct; letter unity, genre, opponents, and sequence remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Makes reputation claims reviewable and rejects leader-controlled testimonials as sufficient accountability.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul's defense responds to evaluation rather than occupying an uncontested status.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Forensic and apologetic models illuminate the defense but do not make Paul's own account neutral.

temporal_scope.notes: Compositional and rhetorical reconstructions remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Introduces the self-commendation issue later developed in the letter.
Directly contests comparison, limits, and approval.

evidence_items.notes: Use independent references, conflict disclosures, and review rather than reputation loops controlled by the subject.

evidence_items.title: Reconciliation begins with divine action
evidence_items.description: Paul attributes reconciliation to God in Messiah and describes a message and ministry entrusted to human agents.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Divine agency and entrusted message are direct; theological, political, and relational models differ.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents mediators from claiming ownership of reconciliation or compelling interpersonal reunion as though they were God.
evidence_items.primary_observation: God is grammatical agent of reconciliation before humans are its messengers.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The passage's divine-human reconciliation cannot be collapsed into every damaged human relationship or a universal mediation script.

temporal_scope.notes: Modern interpersonal transfer requires consent and safety distinctions.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly distinguishes divine reconciling action and human entrusted message.

evidence_items.notes: Do not require private meetings, apologies, touch, shared worship, or restored access as proof of forgiveness.

evidence_items.title: Reciprocal openness is an appeal, not forced disclosure
evidence_items.description: Paul says his speech and heart are open, asks the Corinthians to widen their hearts, and argues that he has wronged, corrupted, and exploited no one.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The appeal and denials are direct; relationship history, letter structure, and recipient assessment remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Distinguishes invited reciprocity from compelled vulnerability, confession, disclosure, or reconciliation.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Openness is rhetorically requested within an active defense.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient psychagogical and apologetic readings clarify persuasion while leaving power imbalance visible.

temporal_scope.notes: The letter preserves Paul's side of the appeal.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly requests reciprocal openness.
Pairs relational appeal with conduct denials and confidence.

evidence_items.notes: A person may decline disclosure, mediation, or contact without being labeled closed-hearted.

evidence_items.title: Retrospective grief language is not a harm method
evidence_items.description: Paul says a prior letter grieved the Corinthians and retrospectively distinguishes grief producing repentance from grief producing death.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The retrospective distinction and reported outcome are direct; psychological causation and letter content are unavailable.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects inducing distress, shame, panic, or trauma as an inherently godly correction technique.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul expresses regret and then joy based on a reported outcome rather than celebrating pain for itself.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Scriptural comfort and grief traditions illuminate the passage, but modern trauma science must not be replaced by exegesis.

temporal_scope.notes: The lost communication and recipients' full experience remain unknown.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly narrates grief, regret, repentance, comfort, and reported outcome.

evidence_items.notes: Do not demand visible tears, rapid confession, or emotional collapse as proof of repentance.

evidence_items.title: Titus mediates knowledge and comfort
evidence_items.description: Titus's arrival, comfort, report, affection, and joy shape Paul's changed understanding of the Corinthian response.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Titus's mediating role is explicit; exact chronology and the report's completeness remain uncertain.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Makes third-party reporting visible while requiring independent corroboration rather than assuming one envoy's account is complete.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul receives relational information through Titus and responds to it.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The scene can be read as conflict mediation but does not establish confidentiality, neutrality, or a modern investigator role.

temporal_scope.notes: Letter and travel chronology remain reconstructed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly attributes information and comfort to Titus's arrival and report.

evidence_items.notes: A mediator should disclose conflicts of interest, protect privacy, and avoid retaliation or pressure.

evidence_items.title: Warfare imagery targets arguments, not people
evidence_items.description: Paul says the weapons are not fleshly and identifies strongholds with arguments, pretensions, and thoughts.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Metaphorical objects are explicit; ancient siege and rhetorical resonances remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects physical force, militarized ministry, harassment, surveillance, dehumanization, or treating opponents as targets.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The text itself redirects warfare language away from fleshly weapons toward thought and argument.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Rhetorical analysis can clarify aggression and authority without literalizing the metaphor.

temporal_scope.notes: Ancient military imagery is literary evidence, not a use-of-force policy.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly labels the weapons nonfleshly and names arguments and thoughts.

evidence_items.notes: People are not strongholds; protection from retaliation includes online and reputational harassment.

evidence_items.title: The boast is explicitly marked foolish
evidence_items.description: Paul repeatedly asks indulgence for foolish boasting while matching and reversing rival credentials through ancestry, labor, suffering, visions, and weakness.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The self-label and catalogue are direct; irony, compositional location, and rhetorical effect are contested.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents competitive suffering, credentials, visions, or institutional growth from becoming unquestionable authority proofs.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Boasting is used and simultaneously disavowed as foolish speech.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Apologetic and honor-shame readings illuminate the strategy while preserving its tension and risks.

temporal_scope.notes: Letter unity and opponent reconstruction remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly marks the speech foolish while deploying competitive boasts.

evidence_items.notes: No hardship story, miracle claim, audience size, or title defeats independent safeguarding review.

evidence_items.title: Rival-apostle labels are partisan evidence
evidence_items.description: Paul uses severe labels for rivals but supplies no neutral dossier establishing their identity, ethnicity, motives, or every alleged practice.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The labels are direct; virtually every social identification of the rivals remains disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents polemical naming from becoming collective blame, guilt by association, or a substitute for evidence.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The rivals are known through the rhetoric of their opponent in a damaged relationship.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Jewish-Christian, intragentile, rhetorical, and missionary-rival reconstructions compete and must not be collapsed.

temporal_scope.notes: Absent opponent voices sharply limit identification.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The polemical labels occur here while neutral identities remain absent.
Comparison with so-called super-apostles remains part of Paul's defense.

evidence_items.notes: Do not infer ethnic guilt, demonic identity, criminality, or abuse findings from rhetorical labels alone.

evidence_items.title: The thorn remains unidentified and uncured
evidence_items.description: Paul reports an unidentified thorn, an unanswered removal request, sufficient grace, and power made complete in weakness.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The nonidentification and no-cure narrative are explicit; medical, social, spiritual, and rhetorical identifications remain speculative.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Resists diagnosis from text, cure promises, disability stigma, and leader claims that weakness proves immunity.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The passage withholds the thorn's identity and turns attention to grace and weakness.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Proposals range from illness to opponents or spiritual assault; none should be presented as certain.

temporal_scope.notes: Modern diagnosis is impossible and inappropriate.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly leaves the thorn unidentified and narrates no removal.

evidence_items.notes: Provide medical care, accommodation, privacy, and role review without treating disability as sin or spiritual superiority.

evidence_items.title: Being spent is a first-person claim
evidence_items.description: Paul says he will spend and be spent for the Corinthians while defending his material practice and contested love.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The self-reference is direct; financial history, irony, and relational effect remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Keeps voluntary self-description from becoming compulsory overwork, unpaid labor, self-neglect, or exploitation of caregivers.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul describes his own intended expenditure rather than issuing a workforce rule.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Parental and financial rhetoric can express commitment while also carrying power that needs ethical scrutiny.

temporal_scope.notes: Ancient economic relations remain partly reconstructed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The spending language is explicitly first-person and relational.

evidence_items.notes: Fair pay, rest, leave, health care, accessibility, and freedom to resign remain required.

evidence_items.title: Signs do not create apostolic immunity
evidence_items.description: Paul appeals to endurance, signs, wonders, and mighty works while also saying he is nothing and defending himself before the community.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The credential appeal and self-lowering language are direct; the signs' nature and rhetorical function remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects miracles, endurance, office, or spiritual fruit as reasons to bypass allegations, evidence, safety measures, or independent review.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Credential rhetoric occurs inside, not outside, a contested accountability relationship.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient apostolic-sign readings vary; no reading makes charism a conduct exemption.

temporal_scope.notes: The passage is not a modern credentialing policy.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins claimed signs, endurance, comparison, and self-lowering.

evidence_items.notes: Leader or institutional reputation must never be a reason to suppress harm.

evidence_items.title: Witness language is not a complete procedure
evidence_items.description: Before a prospective third visit Paul invokes the Deuteronomic two-or-three-witness formula and warns that he will not spare.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The formula and warning are direct; whether witnesses are people, visits, or another referent and how process worked remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Supports evidentiary seriousness while requiring modern notice, impartiality, corroboration appropriate to evidence type, appeal, and protection against intimidation.
evidence_items.primary_observation: A scriptural witness formula is deployed in an impending confrontation.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The passage does not describe investigation, testimony handling, credibility assessment, or trauma-informed interviewing.

temporal_scope.notes: Procedural reconstruction is uncertain.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly invokes witness language while leaving a full adjudication protocol unstated.

evidence_items.notes: Do not mechanically demand multiple victims or eyewitnesses for harms commonly occurring in private.

evidence_items.title: Testing and restoration close the conflict letter
evidence_items.description: The Corinthians are told to examine and test themselves, while Paul prays for their restoration and ends with restoration, comfort, peace, and mutual greeting.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Testing and restoration vocabulary is direct; compositional unity and exact force remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Places communities and leaders under self-examination while orienting action toward repair rather than domination.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Warning does not erase the closing restoration and peace horizon.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Restoration can mean mending or putting in order without implying immediate reinstatement, trust, or contact.

temporal_scope.notes: Letter sequence and unity remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins testing, restoration, comfort, shared mind, and peace.

evidence_items.notes: Peace cannot be purchased by suppressing evidence, survivor voice, dissent, or just consequences.

evidence_items.title: Galatian curse rhetoric is high-intensity boundary speech
evidence_items.description: Paul expresses astonishment at desertion and twice pronounces a curse on anyone proclaiming a contrary gospel.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The curse and boundary claim are direct; opponent identity, rhetorical genre, and transfer remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Marks perceived stakes without licensing threats, harassment, damnation campaigns, or treating disagreement itself as abuse.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The opening deploys severe polemic before the letter's autobiographical defense.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Crisis and curse-rhetoric models explain intensity but do not turn Paul's partisan judgment into a modern finding process.

temporal_scope.notes: Audience geography, date, and opponents remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly contains astonishment, rival-gospel language, and repeated curse.

evidence_items.notes: Do not use curse rhetoric to incite social, economic, digital, or physical punishment.

evidence_items.title: Paul discloses former religious violence
evidence_items.description: Paul says he violently persecuted and tried to destroy God's assembly while advancing in ancestral traditions.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The autobiographical admission is direct; chronology and relation to Acts remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents zeal, pedigree, dramatic conversion, or later office from erasing prior harm or the need for accountability.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Former violence is part of Paul's own authority narrative rather than hidden from readers.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The disclosure supports transformation claims but does not provide the harmed communities' accounts or a full repair record.

temporal_scope.notes: Earlier acts are narrated retrospectively by Paul.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Paul directly reports his earlier violence from a later letter.

evidence_items.notes: Changed behavior does not entitle a person to forgiveness, platform, access, or contact from those harmed.

evidence_items.title: Recognition is negotiated, not absolute
evidence_items.description: Paul says recognized leaders added nothing to him while also reporting a private presentation, Titus's noncompulsion, perceived grace, partnership recognition, differentiated mission, and poor care.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The elements are explicit in Paul's account; date, visit correlation, power dynamics, and other participants' views remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Keeps authority relational and negotiated while resisting both leader absolutism and claims of total independence.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Noncompulsion, disagreement, recognition, differentiation, and shared obligation coexist.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The account cannot be reduced to a modern board meeting or used to erase Titus's agency and gentile stakes.

temporal_scope.notes: Correlation with Acts 11 or 15 remains disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Earlier negotiated events are narrated in the direct letter.

evidence_items.notes: Recognition does not eliminate conflicts of interest, independent review, or protection of affected minorities.

evidence_items.title: Antioch confrontation is a one-sided public account
evidence_items.description: Paul says he opposed Cephas to his face before all because table withdrawal pressured gentiles, but only Paul's retrospective account survives.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Paul's claim of public confrontation is direct; Cephas's account, motives, audience effects, and outcome are absent.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Names public accountability for public discriminatory impact while refusing to make humiliation the default correction method.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Table practice, fear, withdrawal, group influence, and public speech are linked in Paul's narrative.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The episode is central to justification and Jewish-gentile debates but cannot supply a universal escalation rule.

temporal_scope.notes: Date, relation to Jerusalem meetings, and outcome remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Paul's direct letter narrates an earlier public confrontation.

evidence_items.notes: Choose the least exposing effective response consistent with safety, truth, due process, and public correction of public misinformation.

evidence_items.title: Mutual aggression can consume a community
evidence_items.description: Galatians warns that biting and devouring one another can lead to being consumed and contrasts this with love and Spirit-shaped life.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The animal metaphor and warning are direct; precise conflict referents remain uncertain.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects retaliatory escalation, mobbing, harassment, rumor campaigns, and zero-sum faction logic.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Freedom, service through love, mutual aggression, and Spirit-flesh conflict form one exhortation.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The metaphor targets communal self-destruction without requiring silence about real harm.

temporal_scope.notes: Opponent and audience reconstruction remains disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly contrasts loving service with destructive intracommunal aggression.

evidence_items.notes: Nonretaliation does not prohibit documentation, reporting, boundaries, protective action, or lawful remedy.

evidence_items.title: Restoration requires gentleness and self-watch
evidence_items.description: Those called spiritual are told to restore a person caught in transgression with gentleness while watching themselves against temptation.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Restoration, gentleness, and self-watch are direct; caught language and procedural scope remain discussed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Makes humility and risk of helper misconduct explicit controls on correction.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The restorer is not treated as morally invulnerable.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The mending metaphor supports repair but does not dictate contact, reinstatement, or who conducts a modern investigation.

temporal_scope.notes: Modern process requires role separation and expertise.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins restoration, gentleness, and self-examination.

evidence_items.notes: Accused leaders and close allies should not control intake, evidence, findings, support, or appeal.

evidence_items.title: Burden bearing resists abandonment
evidence_items.description: Galatians commands bearing one another's burdens as fulfillment of Messiah's law.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The mutual command is direct; its relation to individual load language requires contextual distinction.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires material, relational, communication, and access support through conflict rather than isolating reporters, survivors, accused people, families, or caregivers.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Restoration immediately expands into mutual burden bearing.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Mutual aid should not become forced emotional labor or assigning a harmed person responsibility for an offender's rehabilitation.

temporal_scope.notes: Application must preserve consent and role boundaries.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly links restoration context to mutual burden bearing.

evidence_items.notes: Offer independent advocates, practical support, leave, counseling choice, and protection from economic retaliation.

evidence_items.title: Mutual support remains beside self-testing
evidence_items.description: Galatians tells each person to test their own work and carry their own load while also bearing one another's burdens.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Both instructions are direct; lexical relation between burdens and load and precise scope remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Balances mutual support with personal accountability and prevents leaders from transferring responsibility for their conduct to communities or victims.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Self-examination, noncomparison, individual load, and mutual burdens occur in one unit.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The apparent tension can describe differentiated responsibility without atomistic self-reliance.

temporal_scope.notes: Lexical nuance and modern transfer remain bounded.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins restoration, burdens, self-testing, and personal responsibility.

evidence_items.notes: Communal care does not erase individual responsibility, restitution, risk management, or consequences.

evidence_items.title: Rival motives are named without approval
evidence_items.description: Philippians distinguishes goodwill and love from envy, rivalry, selfish ambition, and intent to intensify Paul's affliction, yet Paul rejoices that Messiah is proclaimed.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Mixed motives and Paul's response are direct; actors and relation to other opponents remain uncertain.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Separates a true message from harmful motive and conduct; doctrinal correctness does not defeat conduct review.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul can affirm proclamation content while criticizing the speakers' rivalry and intended harm.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The passage does not require celebrating abuse because beneficial outcomes also occurred.

temporal_scope.notes: Imprisonment location and rival identities remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly distinguishes proclamation content, mixed motives, and intended distress.

evidence_items.notes: Positive impact, conversions, charity, or institutional growth never cancels harm or accountability.

evidence_items.title: Philippian opponents remain unidentified
evidence_items.description: Philippians refers to opponents, dogs, evil workers, mutilation, and enemies of Messiah's cross without enough evidence to identify one stable group.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The rhetoric is direct; identity, ethnicity, location, relation among passages, and actions remain highly disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Prevents antisemitism, collective blame, conspiracy identification, and using polemical labels as misconduct findings.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Different opponent descriptions occur in different argumentative settings.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Jewish, gentile, imperial, libertine, and rhetorical reconstructions compete; the letter cannot bear ethnic generalization.

temporal_scope.notes: Letter unity, provenance, and opponent identity remain disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Names opponents and shared conflict without identifying them.
Supplies severe labels whose relation to earlier opponents is uncertain.

evidence_items.notes: Do not map ancient labels onto Jews, denominations, political groups, critics, reporters, or people who leave.

evidence_items.title: Humility opposes status exploitation
evidence_items.description: Philippians opposes selfish ambition and empty glory with attention to others and Messiah's self-emptying, obedient pattern.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The exhortation and narrative movement are direct; hymn origin, syntax, and christological models remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Applies humility to powerful people first and rejects demanding self-erasure, obedience to abuse, or surrender of safety from vulnerable people.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Community exhortation frames the Messiah passage before and after.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Status-reversal readings support mutuality but must not weaponize kenosis against survivors, workers, or disabled people.

temporal_scope.notes: Christological and compositional debates remain explicit.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly frames Messiah's pattern with anti-rivalry and mutual attention.

evidence_items.notes: Humility is not waiver of rights, reporting, boundaries, medical care, accommodation, pay, or appeal.

evidence_items.title: Euodia and Syntyche receive equal appeal without assigned blame
evidence_items.description: Paul appeals separately to Euodia and Syntyche to share a mind, calls them coworkers who struggled beside him, and asks a third party to help.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Names, parallel appeal, coworker status, and requested help are explicit; conflict content and blame are absent.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Preserves women's mission agency and blocks speculation, gender stereotypes, public blame, or forced reconciliation.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The letter honors both women while addressing an unspecified disagreement.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The scene may involve leadership conflict, but no surviving evidence identifies topic, severity, fault, or resolution.

temporal_scope.notes: The disagreement cannot be reconstructed securely.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly names both women, appeals in parallel, recognizes coworking, and requests help.

evidence_items.notes: Do not reduce named women to a warning about female conflict or assume reconciliation required direct contact.

evidence_items.title: Requested help does not equal compulsory mediation
evidence_items.description: The letter asks a trusted person to help Euodia and Syntyche and then commends gentleness, prayer, and guarded hearts.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The requested assistance and literary sequence are direct; mediator identity and process are disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Supports offered assistance while requiring voluntariness, suitability screening, safety planning, and the right to decline joint meetings.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Third-party help and gentleness appear in close literary proximity.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The text does not describe mediation stages, confidentiality, neutrality, or an outcome.

temporal_scope.notes: The helper's identity and intervention are uncertain.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins requested help with gentleness and care.

evidence_items.notes: Mediation is inappropriate where coercive control, violence, severe power imbalance, active retaliation, or unsafe contact is present.

evidence_items.title: Commendation begins with truth and justice
evidence_items.description: Philippians directs attention toward what is true, honorable, just, pure, pleasing, commendable, excellent, and praiseworthy.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The list is direct; its philosophical resonances and precise semantic boundaries remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Keeps positive communication anchored in truth and justice rather than image management or coerced positivity.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Truth and justice stand inside, not outside, the commendation list.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Moral-philosophical parallels can illuminate vocabulary without turning the list into denial of grief or conflict.

temporal_scope.notes: Direct exhortation with broader ancient moral resonances.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly includes truth and justice among commendable objects of attention.

evidence_items.notes: Do not label reports, lament, anger, or evidence negative merely because they threaten institutional comfort.

evidence_items.title: Bold appeal rejects deceit, flattery, and greed
evidence_items.description: First Thessalonians claims boldness while denying error, impurity, deceit, flattery, greed, and pursuit of human glory.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The denials are direct; accusations, rhetorical convention, and audience assessment are partly reconstructed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires truthful communication and financial transparency while refusing to equate confidence with coercion.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The writers defend both message and manner in relational terms.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient philosophical and apologetic parallels illuminate the defense but do not certify motive by assertion alone.

temporal_scope.notes: The direct letter preserves the writers' defense.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins bold speech with denials of manipulative practice.

evidence_items.notes: Claims of pure motive remain open to evidence, impact assessment, finance review, and correction.

evidence_items.title: Parental metaphors are bounded by gentle self-sharing
evidence_items.description: The writers compare themselves to a nursing caregiver and an exhorting father while recalling self-sharing and labor.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Both metaphors and practices are direct; textual form, gendered resonances, and precise audience composition remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Reads care and exhortation together without granting leaders parental ownership, infantilizing adults, or overriding consent.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Gentleness, affection, self-sharing, labor, encouragement, and parental imagery form the defense.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Moral-philosophical and household parallels clarify rhetoric but cannot establish unrestricted authority.

temporal_scope.notes: Metaphor is not literal kinship or guardianship.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins parental imagery with affection, labor, encouragement, and witness.

evidence_items.notes: Adults retain autonomy, privacy, relationships, finances, medical choice, and the right to leave.

evidence_items.title: Leader esteem remains beside communal testing
evidence_items.description: The community is asked to recognize laboring leaders and live at peace, while nearby instructions require testing everything.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Labor, leadership, esteem, peace, and testing are explicit; office structures and literary relations remain debated.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Keeps respect compatible with questions, discernment, complaints, evidence, and correction.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Leadership recognition occurs within a plural closing exhortation, not as an immunity clause.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The local roles may be emergent rather than a complete later office system.

temporal_scope.notes: Leadership form remains historically uncertain.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Places leader recognition, peace, differentiated care, and testing in one exhortation.

evidence_items.notes: Esteem is not secrecy, blind obedience, non-disparagement, or surrender of appeal rights.

evidence_items.title: Different needs receive different responses
evidence_items.description: The community is told to admonish the disorderly, encourage the fainthearted, support the weak, and be patient with everyone.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The differentiated verbs are direct; the groups, conditions, and ancient practices remain uncertain.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects one-size-fits-all discipline and requires distinguishing misconduct, distress, disability, illness, poverty, trauma response, and disagreement.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Correction, encouragement, support, and universal patience are not interchangeable responses.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Ancient paraenesis and philosophical care may clarify terms, but modern assessment requires qualified expertise.

temporal_scope.notes: Identity of the disorderly and fainthearted remains disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly assigns differentiated care and patience.

evidence_items.notes: Do not relabel disability, trauma response, dissent, unemployment, or communication difference as rebellion.

evidence_items.title: Prophecy is welcomed and tested
evidence_items.description: First Thessalonians joins nonquenching and noncontempt for prophecy with testing everything and retaining the good.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Both openness and testing are direct; testing agents and criteria are not fully specified.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects both automatic dismissal and automatic acceptance of claimed revelation.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Spiritual openness and critical discernment are simultaneous commands.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The text supports communal evaluation but not a leader-controlled process or replacement of evidence.

temporal_scope.notes: Local criteria and roles remain unstated.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Directly joins prophecy reception, testing, retention, and avoidance.

evidence_items.notes: A prophecy cannot decide guilt, require secrecy, block medical care, compel a relationship, or defeat a person's refusal.

evidence_items.title: Acts council is a later narrative comparator
evidence_items.description: Acts narrates dispute, testimony, scriptural argument, deliberation, a letter, and delegates concerning gentile inclusion.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The narrative sequence is direct; speech historicity and relation to Galatians 2 remain disputed.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Adds a later literary model of collective deliberation without overwriting Galatians' earlier first-person conflict account.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Multiple voices and a written communication appear in Acts' narrated resolution.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Acts may preserve memory while shaping a more orderly unity narrative; it is not a verbatim meeting record.

temporal_scope.notes: Narrated event and source composition are separated; Galatians correlation remains disputed.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Later narrative comparison must not silently settle the earlier direct-letter chronology.

evidence_items.notes: Do not present narrated unanimity as proof that every participant consented or every harm was resolved.

evidence_items.title: Acts leaves a coworker rupture unresolved
evidence_items.description: Acts reports a sharp disagreement between Paul and Barnabas over John Mark and separate travel teams without declaring one party morally right.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: The rupture and separate journeys are direct; motives, private process, and later repair are not narrated here.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Allows safe separation and continued vocation without inventing blame or forcing a reconciliation scene.
evidence_items.primary_observation: The narrative reports division and new teams rather than a tidy resolution.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Later canonical references to Barnabas or Mark do not narrate this conflict's process and should not be used to manufacture one.

temporal_scope.notes: Later narrative composition and earlier narrated event remain distinct.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Later narrative comparison preserves separation without a narrated reconciliation.

evidence_items.notes: Not every working relationship can or should be restored; safe separation can be a legitimate outcome.

evidence_items.title: Correction must not become coercive control
evidence_items.description: Modern conflict practice distinguishes bounded, transparent correction from patterns that dominate conscience, movement, relationships, money, work, health care, communication, or exit.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Ancient non-domination, gentleness, and self-watch controls are direct; modern transfer requires current trauma and legal expertise.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires safety, voice, choice, clear authority limits, written process, support persons, and an unpenalized right to decline or leave.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul denies lordship over faith and requires gentle restoration with self-examination.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: SAMHSA's safety, trustworthiness, collaboration, empowerment, voice, and choice principles expose coercive misuse in modern institutions.

temporal_scope.narrative_setting: Ancient correction texts in modern reception
temporal_scope.notes: Use current law and qualified local safeguarding and trauma expertise.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Ancient non-domination language is an ethical control, not a complete modern policy.
Gentleness and self-watch constrain modern correction.

evidence_items.notes: Correction never authorizes threats of damnation, family loss, poverty, exposure, deportation, job loss, or medical neglect.

evidence_items.title: Boundaries must not become shunning or deprivation
evidence_items.description: A community may use proportionate participation boundaries, but coordinated ostracism, livelihood loss, housing pressure, family cutoff, aid denial, medical neglect, blacklisting, and surveillance create additional harms.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Ancient boundary and reassessment texts are clear but incomplete; modern material consequences require rights-based analysis.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires written scope, essential-needs protection, time limits, review, appeal, and prohibition of retaliation beyond the legitimate setting.
evidence_items.primary_observation: First Corinthians presents a specified boundary; Second Corinthians later presents sufficient action, forgiveness, comfort, and reaffirmed love.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The ancient texts do not authorize total social death or deprivation, and ILO standards clarify protection from retaliation and access to remedy.

temporal_scope.narrative_setting: Ancient boundary texts in modern institutional reception
temporal_scope.notes: Current law and local material-risk assessment govern practice.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The case-bound ancient action cannot be expanded into total deprivation.
Sufficiency and changed action require revisability.

evidence_items.notes: Protect dependents and uninvolved family members; never condition essential aid on compliance, apology, silence, or renewed contact.

evidence_items.title: Forgiveness does not compel reconciliation or contact
evidence_items.description: Forgiveness, divine reconciliation, interpersonal reconciliation, restored trust, restitution, office, access, and contact answer different questions and may follow different timelines.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Pauline vocabulary and case movement are inspectable; exact modern distinctions require trauma-aware ethical and legal judgment.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Protects a survivor's right to distance, indirect communication, no joint meeting, no touch, no shared worship, and no restoration of access.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Second Corinthians uses forgiveness, comfort, reaffirmed love, and divine reconciliation in distinct contexts.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: Trauma-informed safety, voice, and choice prevent these terms from becoming tools of compelled reunion.

temporal_scope.narrative_setting: Ancient forgiveness and reconciliation in modern reception
temporal_scope.notes: Safety plans and lawful protective orders take precedence over institutional reunion goals.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The ancient restorative case does not specify a harmed person's contact duty.
Divine reconciliation cannot be collapsed into compulsory human reunion.

evidence_items.notes: No public apology, sacrament, counseling session, or leader declaration can require restored trust or access.

evidence_items.title: Confidentiality must not conceal danger
evidence_items.description: Confidentiality protects privacy and fair process, but secrecy that hides danger, blocks reporting, destroys records, coordinates stories, or protects reputation is concealment.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Pauline reports show mediated and incomplete information; modern privacy and reporting duties require current legal expertise.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires data minimization, informed privacy limits, secure records, need-to-know access, lawful reporting, and transparent conflict-of-interest handling.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Chloe's people and Titus carry reports that affect communal conflict, while the letters disclose only selected details.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: ILO Convention 190 protects privacy while explicitly warning that confidentiality requirements must not be misused.

temporal_scope.narrative_setting: Ancient reporting channels in modern reception
temporal_scope.notes: Mandatory-reporting and privacy law vary by jurisdiction; use qualified advice.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Named reporting does not itself define modern disclosure limits.
Mediated reporting illustrates information dependence and incompleteness.

evidence_items.notes: Leader or institutional reputation is never a valid reason to suppress harm, intimidate reporters, or withhold required notice.

evidence_items.title: Due process requires proportionate and revisable action
evidence_items.description: A fair process identifies allegations and authority, provides notice and meaningful response, separates support from investigation, manages conflicts, documents evidence and reasons, protects all parties, and allows review and correction.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Witness, testing, sufficiency, and restoration language offer analogies; modern procedural design comes from current law and safeguarding practice.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires impartial fact-finding, accessible participation, evidence-type-sensitive corroboration, proportionate interim measures, written outcomes, appeal, and revision when facts change.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Pauline texts invoke witnesses, testing, a sufficient prior action, changed community response, and restoration.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: No selected passage supplies a full adjudication code; ILO standards add safe, fair, effective internal and external mechanisms.

temporal_scope.narrative_setting: Ancient testing and restoration texts in modern governance
temporal_scope.notes: Use current civil, criminal, employment, child-protection, privacy, and disability law.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Witness and testing language supplies an analogy, not a complete procedure.
Testing and retaining the good require evaluation rather than automatic acceptance.

evidence_items.notes: Do not require multiple victims for private harm, confuse a safety measure with a guilt finding, or promise confidentiality that law cannot permit.

evidence_items.title: Conflict communication should resist retraumatization
evidence_items.description: Trauma-informed practice recognizes trauma effects and embeds physical and psychological safety, trustworthiness, transparency, collaboration, peer support, empowerment, voice, choice, and cultural humility.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: SAMHSA states the modern framework; applying it to religious conflict requires qualified contextual judgment.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires predictable contact, informed consent, safe pacing, communication choice, support persons, breaks, accessible formats, and avoidance of surprise confrontation or compelled narrative repetition.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul retrospectively reports anguish, tears, grief, comfort, and a changed relationship but offers no modern trauma model.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: SAMHSA's framework supplies current safeguards without retrodiagnosing Paul or the Corinthians.

temporal_scope.narrative_setting: Ancient grief texts in modern conflict reception
temporal_scope.notes: Use qualified trauma, medical, mental-health, cultural, and safeguarding expertise.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: Ancient grief and restoration language needs trauma-aware transfer.
Retrospective grief claims cannot justify inducing distress.

evidence_items.notes: A calm demeanor is not proof of truth, and distress, fragmented memory, delayed disclosure, or communication difference is not proof of falsehood.

evidence_items.title: Reporting must be independent and protected from retaliation
evidence_items.description: Safe systems provide channels outside the accused person's authority, external options, conflict disclosure, timely triage, support, secure records, protection for complainants and witnesses, and remedies for retaliation.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Modern ILO standards are explicit; Pauline reporting episodes reveal information networks but not a complete system.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Rejects accused leaders receiving sole reports, selecting investigators, controlling communications, funding silence, threatening status, or retaliating through sermons, references, work, housing, aid, immigration, or social networks.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul depends on named and delegated reporters within contested relationships.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: ILO Convention 190 calls for safe, fair, effective internal and external mechanisms, support, privacy, and protection against victimization and retaliation.

temporal_scope.narrative_setting: Ancient reporting texts in modern governance
temporal_scope.notes: Local reporting duties and whistleblower protections vary; use qualified legal advice.

scripture_references.relevance_rationale: The named report illustrates dependence on channels but not their safety.
Titus's mediated report shows the need to assess independence and completeness.

evidence_items.notes: Retaliation includes spiritual threats, outing, defamation, doxxing, exclusion of family, adverse references, immigration pressure, and denial of livelihood or care.

evidence_items.title: Accessible restoration never requires forced contact
evidence_items.description: Equitable processes provide disability and communication access, procedural accommodation, chosen support, safe pacing, and restoration paths compatible with permanent separation or indirect contact.
evidence_items.confidence_rationale: Pauline mutual-honor and restoration texts provide ethical controls; current disability and trauma standards govern implementation.
evidence_items.passage_relevance: Requires accessible notices and interviews, interpreters, alternative formats, sensory and mobility access, remote or asynchronous participation, breaks, support persons, and no forced encounter.
evidence_items.primary_observation: Paul assigns greater honor and care to members deemed weaker and joins restoration to gentleness and revisable community response.
evidence_items.scholarly_interpretation: The CRPD protects equal recognition, accessibility, communication, access to justice, and freedom from exploitation, violence, and abuse; SAMHSA adds safety, voice, and choice.
